# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] held(N1) -> le(ep(N2), ep(N1))

invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant held(N) -> le(ep(X), ep(N))
invariant transfer(E, N) & ~le(E, ep(N)) -> ~le(E, ep(X))
invariant ~(held(N1) & transfer(E, N2) & ~le(E, ep(N2)))
invariant transfer(E1, N1) & ~le(E1, ep(N1)) & transfer(E2, N2) & ~le(E2, ep(N2)) -> E1 = E2 & N1 = N2
invariant locked(E, N) -> le(E, ep(N))
invariant held(N) & ep(N) ~= zero -> locked(ep(N), N)
invariant locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant transfer(E, N) & ~le(E, ep(N)) -> ~locked(E, X)
invariant locked(E, N) -> E ~= zero

# Figure 4

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node
individual firste:epoch
axiom firste ~= zero

    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := firste if N = first else zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
#    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

invariant transfer(E, N) -> ~le(E, firste)

invariant held(N) & ep(N) = firste -> N = first
invariant ep(N) ~= zero & (N ~= first | ep(N) ~= firste) -> transfer(ep(N), N)

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node
individual firste:epoch
axiom firste ~= zero

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := firste if N = first else zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
#    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node
individual firste:epoch
axiom firste ~= zero

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := firste if N = first else zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
#    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant transfer(E, N1) & transfer(E, N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant locked(E, N) -> transfer(E, N)
invariant held(N) & transfer(E, N2) -> le(E, ep(N))
invariant transfer(E1, N1) & transfer(E2, N2) & ~le(E2, E1) -> locked(E1, N1)
invariant held(N) & ep(N) = E & E ~= firste -> locked(E, N)
invariant held(N) & ep(N) = firste -> N = first
invariant transfer(E, N) & ep(N2) = E & held(N2) -> N = N2
invariant transfer(E, N) & ep(N2) = E & locked(E, N2) -> N = N2
invariant ep(N) ~= zero -> le(firste, ep(N))
invariant transfer(E, N) -> le(firste, E)
invariant locked(E, N) -> le(E, ep(N))
invariant locked(E, N) -> ~le(E, zero)
invariant transfer(E, N) -> ~le(E, zero)
invariant ep(N) = E & E ~= zero & (N ~= first | E ~= firste) -> transfer(E, N)

**Verifying Epoch Transitions**

I'm now focusing on the epoch and transfer message interactions. My analysis is on proving that a `locked` message for a specific epoch can only be issued if a corresponding `transfer` for that same epoch has been accepted, ensuring the protocol's integrity.

**Refining Transfer Conditions**

I'm now investigating the conditions surrounding transfer messages and their relationship with lock holdings. Specifically, I'm working to prove that any 'transfer' message for a given epoch must correspond to an epoch less than or equal to the currently held lock's epoch.

**Confirming Token State Transitions**

I'm now verifying that a `grant` event correctly transitions the token state. Specifically, I've confirmed that once a lock is granted, it is marked as `held` false until an `accept` event occurs, ensuring no concurrent holdings.

**Refining Invariants**

I'm refining the protocol invariants based on new observations. Specifically, I've identified an error in a previous invariant regarding held tokens and transfers, and I'm formulating new ones to accurately capture the relationships between epoch numbers and token holdings, particularly concerning sequential transfer acceptances.

**Validating Held State Uniqueness**

I'm focusing on proving the uniqueness of the `held` state. My current analysis indicates that an `accept` operation requires the transfer epoch to be strictly greater than the current token epoch, which I believe, along with previous invariants, should implicitly guarantee only one token can be held at any given time.

**Proving Held State Uniqueness**

I'm rigorously proving that only one token can be held at any point. My current focus is on the implication that if a token is held, any subsequent transfer must be for an epoch less than or equal to the currently held token's epoch, reinforcing the uniqueness invariant.

I'm re-evaluating invariant `invar15` after a surprising failure. The counterexample suggests my previous understanding of the relationship between `transfer` and `locked` events was flawed, prompting a revision of its definition.

**Revising Accept Logic**

I'm re-examining the `accept` action's conditional logic. It seems my understanding of the `~le(e, ep(n))` condition was incorrect in light of the counterexample, as it prevents state changes when `e <= ep(n)`, which is precisely what the failure implies.

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node
individual firste:epoch
axiom firste ~= zero

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := firste if N = first else zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
#    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant transfer(E, N1) & transfer(E, N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant locked(E, N) -> transfer(E, N)
invariant held(N) & ep(N) = E & E ~= firste -> locked(E, N)
invariant held(N) & ep(N) = firste -> N = first
invariant transfer(E, N) -> ~le(E, firste)
invariant ep(N) ~= zero -> le(firste, ep(N))
invariant held(N) & transfer(E, N2) -> le(E, ep(N))
invariant transfer(E1, N1) & transfer(E2, N2) & ~le(E2, E1) -> locked(E1, N1)
invariant transfer(E, N) & ep(N2) = E & held(N2) -> N = N2
invariant transfer(E, N) & ep(N2) = E & locked(E, N2) -> N = N2
invariant ep(N) = E & E ~= zero & (N ~= first | E ~= firste) -> transfer(E, N)
invariant locked(E, N) -> le(E, ep(N))
invariant transfer(E, N) -> ~le(E, zero)
invariant locked(E, N) -> ~le(E, zero)
invariant transfer(E1, N1) & held(N2) & ep(N2) = E2 & ~le(E1, E2) -> false
invariant transfer(E1, N1) & transfer(E2, N2) & ~le(E1, E2) -> locked(E2, N2)
invariant locked(E, N) & transfer(E, N2) -> N = N2
